newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA TO BORROW TWICE ON INT'L MARKETS IN 97.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA TO BORROW TWICE ON INT'L MARKETS IN 97.

text.p: Lithuania, which is set to launch a $200 million eurobond later this year, will probably tap the international capital markets one more time in 1997, a senior finance ministry official said.

"After the eurobond, we will probably go to the (international) market again in 1997," Ruta Skyriene, the deputy director of the international department in Lithuania's finance ministry, told Reuters in an interview.
She added that the government was still weighing its options.
"It could be another eurobond issue or maybe a yankee. We can't say for sure at this point," she said.

Lithuania's budget law prohibits the country's foreign debt from rising by more than $600 million in 1997. The figure stood at $1.2 billion at the end of 1996 or 16.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Lithuania announced last Friday that JP Morgan Securities would be the lead manager for the eurobond issue.
Lithuania, which has already acquired credit ratings from Moody's and IBCA, will seek another from Standard and Poor's before it issues the bond.
Skyriene said the finance ministry was confident that the rating would be favourable.
"Our main strengths include the political situation...all of the major parties support reform, and Lithuania does not have any minorities problems or big conflicts with Russia," she said.
"Lithuania's foreign debt and borrowing needs are very modest and fiscal policy is very tight," she added.
